item.title: Calibration of Passive Market Impact with a Queue-Sensitive Propagator Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.38442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a framework for calibrating passive market impact, defined as the price response to liquidity-providing limit orders, in contrast to the impact of liquidity-consuming market orders. We build on the model of Ouazzani Chahdi, Rosenbaum, and Szymanski (arxiv:2412.07461), which combines Hawkes-driven market-order flow with queue-reactive limit-order and cancellation dynamics. Within this model, we show that the price decomposes into a universal propagator term driven by signed order-flow imbalance and a state-dependent correction that captures the dependence of price sensitivity on volume at the best quotes. This decomposition links limit-order-book microstructure to standard propagator models and yields a regression on two observable signals: the propagator signal and the queue-weighted order-flow imbalance. We calibrate the model on high-frequency order-book data and find that the passive-impact term explains substantial variation in prices beyond the classical propagator, improving both model fit and the accuracy of predicted impact curves.
item.dc:creator: Yadh Hafsi, Fabrizio Lillo, Gr\'egoire Szymanski

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Implicit Diversification Regularisers for Cross-Sectional Cryptocurrency Returns
item.description: arXiv:2610.39205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Factor models are central to asset pricing and portfolio construction, but neural factors are often difficult to interpret, and their effect on portfolio risk is unclear. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) may address both concerns by describing daily returns across many assets with only a few active features. We ask whether this sparse representation produces stable financial factors and better-diversified portfolios. We study cryptocurrency returns, use equities as a secondary test, and compare the SAE with common benchmarks in a time-ordered evaluation. We find consistently lower volatility in SAE portfolios and link this result to lower correlations among the selected assets. However, the SAE does not outperform a simple contrarian strategy on risk-adjusted return, and its factor identities are not stable across training runs. Our contribution is to show that sparse coding can support portfolio diversification, while clearly separating this risk effect from claims about alpha or stable factor identities.
item.dc:creator: Weijia Han, Lisha Qu

item.title: Depth-Efficient Quantum Topological Data Analysis for Regime-Specific Detection of Financial Stress
item.description: arXiv:2607.09906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present, to our knowledge, the first adaptation of Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) to quantum topological data analysis, reformulating Betti number estimation as a depth-efficient variational optimization over a compressed qubit register. From a Takens embedding and Vietoris-Rips filtration of S&P 500 returns, we extract combinatorial Laplacians and recast null-space counting as a continuous-PCE Rayleigh-quotient minimization with variational deflation, encoding $n_k$ simplex indices into $O(n_k^{1/\kappa})$ qubits with shallow, ancilla-free circuits. Because the resulting loss is rational rather than bilinear in the correlators, the barren-plateau bound of Sciorilli et al. does not transfer; empirically the gradient variance decays only polynomially, with no exponential barren plateau, over $n=4$-$12$ qubits. The classical stage matches ripser on all 190 sliding windows (2003-2010). On the real market Laplacians ($\beta_1=1$-$22$), PCE-VQE recovers no null vector from a random start, but warm-starting from a classical null-space surrogate recovers $\beta_1$ exactly on all seven windows tested ($n_k \le 259$), placing the obstacle in the optimization landscape rather than the encoding. Chronologically split classification gives in-regime ROC AUC 0.818, but out-of-distribution evaluation on the 2020 COVID shock and 2022 rate cycle (AUC 0.009, 0.515) shows the calibration does not generalize across crisis regimes.
item.dc:creator: Arul Rhik Mazumder, Shreyan Ronit Mazumder
